response: PokerBench handles post-flop vastness by grouping the enormous board space into 11 hand-designed board textures, so strategically similar community-card configurations are evaluated together. LSPO (Werewolf) handles unbounded dialogue by mapping free-form utterances into a finite latent strategy space, creating an abstracted extensive-form game for optimization. In both cases, the goal is tractability via abstraction: PokerBench compresses many similar poker boards into texture classes, while LSPO compresses many possible language actions into latent strategy categories. The main difference is that PokerBench abstracts game states for evaluation, whereas LSPO abstracts actions/utterances for policy learning and game-theoretic optimization.
judge_justification: The response correctly compares the two abstraction methods: PokerBench groups similar post-flop boards into 11 hand-designed texture classes to make the board space tractable, while LSPO maps free-form dialogue into a finite latent strategy space via embedding/clustering for optimization. It captures the shared idea of dimensionality reduction/abstraction and clearly distinguishes the different domains and purposes.
